prompt_summaries.name: Dataset Inspection + Schema Mapping
prompt_summaries.summary: All 3 real Bank CSVs map cleanly onto the canonical schema with 0 rejected rows and 0 zero-amount rows (confirming a previously-fixed credit-column keyword bug stays fixed). Found: 1 ambiguous debit+credit row in the primary file (B1-1); ~15.7% missing balance values including the first row in the savings file (B1-2); 3 real, clean columns (value_date/channel/transaction_reference) not captured by ingestion in 2 of 3 files (B1-3). No currency or account-number columns in any file (handled gracefully via fallbacks). Verdict: PASS (primary, wallet), PASS WITH ISSUES (savings).

prompt_summaries.name: Ingestion Testing
prompt_summaries.summary: All 3 files ingested with 0 rows rejected (465/1,670/8,158 rows respectively). is_anomalous flagging confirmed precise (0 false positives) via a real contextual marker. Found: is_own_account_transfer detection exists but is never auto-wired into ingestion (B2-1); no duplicate-ingestion protection at all, confirmed via both an accidental crash-orphan and an intentional re-ingestion (B2-2); balance-integrity fails for savings (discrepancy 32.76) and wallet (800,624.14, the worst of the three despite wallet having the most complete balance data) (B2-3); account_number_hash falls back to an upload-id-derived hash since no file has a real account number, so re-uploads are never recognized as the same account (B2-4). Verdict: PASS WITH ISSUES for all 3 files.

prompt_summaries.name: Dashboard Endpoint Testing
prompt_summaries.summary: compute_dashboard_summary's arithmetic (inflows, outflows, credit/debit counts) matched independent SQL recomputation exactly for all 5 accounts tested (3 canonical + 2 duplicate copies of the primary file). Response envelope confirmed correct. Found: is_own_account_transfer false positives (rooted in B2-1/B2-2) severely corrupt the savings account's dashboard -- 100% of its 933 real debits are wrongly excluded, reporting 0 outflows instead of the real 3,794,287.92 (B3-1, Critical); the same contamination affects the wallet account at ~4.2%; balance-integrity failures (B2-3) are invisible from this endpoint's output (B3-2); dashboard/summary has no disabled_features implementation at all (B3-3). Verdict: FAIL for the savings account specifically (dashboard output itself factually wrong); PASS WITH ISSUES for primary/wallet.

prompt_summaries.name: Diagnostics Endpoint Testing
prompt_summaries.summary: All 5 diagnostic endpoints (income-stability, abm, cashflow-analysis, customer-segmentation, revenue-patterns) implemented, RBAC-gated, and envelope-correct. 11 direct value comparisons against independent recomputation across all 3 accounts, 0 mismatches. Confirmed B3-1 propagates into cashflow-analysis/customer-segmentation for the savings account as expected (not a new defect). Found: ABM's trend label is sign-incorrect for accounts with a negative 12-month average balance -- the primary account's genuinely worsening trend is labeled 'improving' (B4-1, High); 3 of 5 diagnostics silently return null/empty instead of using the proper disabled_features mechanism for insufficient data (B4-2, Low). Verdict: PASS WITH ISSUES.

prompt_summaries.name: Predictive Model Testing
prompt_summaries.summary: All 3 predictive endpoints (fraud-risk, loan-readiness, cashflow-forecast) implemented and RBAC-gated; fraud-risk and loan-readiness scores hand-recomputed from their component parts and matched exactly, including a cross-endpoint consistency check. PaySim fraud-dataset compatibility confirmed genuinely Not Implemented (incompatible column schema), not worked around. Found: cash-runway calculation produces backwards-appearing results for already-overdrawn accounts (B5-1, High); loan-readiness scores a zero-transaction account as perfectly creditworthy, 100/Tier A, because compute_fraud_risk has no minimum-data floor (B5-2, Critical); B4-1's ABM mislabeling confirmed to inflate the primary account's loan-readiness score by the full 25-point abm_trend weight and suppress a legitimate recommendation (B5-3, High, cross-referenced to B4-1); B1-1's ambiguous row plausibly explains a fraud-risk statement-integrity failure (B5-4, Low, cross-referenced to B1-1). Verdict: PASS WITH ISSUES.

prompt_summaries.name: AI Layer Testing
prompt_summaries.summary: Both AI endpoints (lender-brief, financial-health-playbook) exist, are reachable, and return schema-valid AIRecommendation objects (20 recommendations checked, 0 schema failures) inside the correct response envelope. Every non-AI-generated numeric field in both endpoints matched real Prompt 3/4/5 reference values exactly across all 3 accounts, including faithful propagation of B4-1/B5-2/B5-3/B3-1/B2-3/B5-4 into the AI-facing documents. No hallucinations of financial fact found in any AI narrative text across 20 recommendations; in one case the model self-diagnosed the B5-2 defect unprompted. Found: lender-brief's own AI recommendation section failed in 4/4 real Gemini calls tested due to an 8-second-per-attempt timeout bug that is effectively guaranteed to fail given this environment's real response latency (B6-1, Critical); the required revenue_at_stake field is fabricated with no traceable basis whenever the account's data offers no natural anchor value (B6-2, Medium); created_at is never grounded to real generation time (B6-3, Low); the lender-brief endpoint has no disabled_features signaling at all, compounding B5-2's inflated zero-transaction score with the least guardrail messaging of any Bank endpoint tested (B6-4, Medium). Verdict: PASS WITH ISSUES.

root_cause_groups.explanation: B2-1 (detection never auto-wired into ingestion) and B2-2 (no duplicate-ingestion protection) compound directly into B3-1, the most severe unresolved issue found across all 6 prompts: up to 100% of a real account's outflows suppressed by false-positive transfer flags. B2-4 (hash-based account fallback) worsens this by preventing the system from even recognizing repeat uploads of the same account after the fact. This root cause propagated forward into every subsequent prompt's results for the savings account (dashboard, 2 diagnostics, 2 predictive components, both AI endpoints).

A source-data/derivation gap (root cause never determined) causes 2 of 3 real files to fail balance reconciliation. This is invisible from the dashboard endpoint specifically (B3-2), but is correctly, consistently surfaced as an informational 'failed' flag in fraud-risk and the lender-brief through Prompt 6, with no incorrect score ever resulting from it.

A single sign-handling bug in compute_abm's trend-label formula (specific to negative 12-month baselines) was first observed as a diagnostic-display issue (B4-1), then confirmed to have a quantified, material effect on the loan-readiness composite score (B5-3), then confirmed to appear unchanged and uncaveated in the customer/lender-facing lender-brief document (Prompt 6).

compute_fraud_risk's lack of a minimum-data floor causes an account with zero transactions to score as maximally creditworthy (B5-2). This is compounded, not caught, at the AI layer: the lender-brief endpoint has no disabled_features mechanism at all to warn a reader that the perfect score comes from an account with no verifiable history (B6-4) -- notably, the sibling financial-health-playbook endpoint's own AI-generated text independently recognized and flagged this exact risk when given the chance, showing the gap is structural (missing warning plumbing) rather than a model limitation.
An isolated defect: the cash-runway formula was never designed for an already-negative starting balance. Confirmed not to share a root cause with, or propagate into, any other issue or the AI layer.

root_cause_groups.group: AI dependency / Gemini integration reliability and field grounding
root_cause_groups.explanation: A timeout-handling bug in the shared Gemini client (per-attempt rather than total budget) causes one specific caller (lender-brief, with its tighter 8s budget) to fail deterministically while its sibling (financial-health-playbook, 30s budget) succeeds reliably with the identical prompt template. Separately, two required AIRecommendation fields (revenue_at_stake, created_at) have no defined grounding methodology in the shared prompt template, so the model fabricates plausible values whenever it lacks a real anchor -- most severe for accounts with the least real data (compounding the same underlying 'thin data' condition that also drives B5-2).

One synthetic-looking anomalous row in the primary file causes an informational integrity-check field ('sequential_ordering') to read 'failed' rather than 'passed'. Confirmed benign for every actual calculation (dashboard, fraud score) that touches this row; the causal link to the sequential_ordering flag itself was never confirmed with row-level certainty.

Several endpoints across the analyzer (dashboard, 3 of 5 diagnostics, lender-brief) never implement the disabled_features/insufficient-data-signaling pattern that income-stability, abm, and financial-health-playbook do use correctly -- an inconsistency in how gracefully different endpoints communicate thin data, not a correctness defect in any single one.

A malformed RBAC row from an earlier, unrelated ad-hoc script in this engagement caused a 403 during Prompt 3 setup. Resolved by adding a correct row alongside it; has no bearing on real application behavior.

Verify is_own_account_transfer / duplicate-ingestion behavior (B2-1/B2-2/B2-4/B3-1) under true multi-merchant, multi-account integration conditions -- this QA pass only observed it under a single manually-triggered global pass across one merchant's accounts; whether the same false-positive pattern occurs, or worsens, across merchant boundaries is Unknown.

Check whether Ecommerce and Sales' own AI playbook endpoints share the same generate_recommendations()/ai_client.py code path with a similarly tight custom timeout (the root cause of B6-1) -- if so, the identical deterministic-failure pattern should be expected there too and is worth confirming during any cross-analyzer AI-layer integration check.

Confirm response-envelope and disabled_features consistency across all three verticals' equivalent endpoints -- this analyzer alone shows the same inconsistency pattern (some endpoints signal insufficient data properly, others silently return nulls) in at least 4 separate places (B3-3, B4-2, B6-4); worth a cross-analyzer sweep rather than treating each vertical's version as independent.

If any merchant-onboarding or new-account integration flow can realistically query loan-readiness or the lender-brief before real transaction history exists, explicitly test against B5-2's zero-transaction-scores-100 behavior before that flow is trusted for any real lending decision.

If Integration testing includes any cross-referencing of accounts by identity (e.g., matching a re-uploaded statement to an existing account), account_number_hash's upload-id-based fallback (B2-4) means this will not work for any of the 3 real Bank file shapes tested here -- confirm whether Integration's matching logic depends on this.
summary: Across all 6 prompts and every dataset tested, every independently-recomputable calculation in the Bank Analyzer -- ingestion row counts, dashboard totals, all 5 diagnostics, all 3 predictive model scores, and every non-AI-generated figure surfaced by the 2 AI endpoints -- matched independent recomputation exactly, with zero arithmetic mismatches found in any prompt. No crashes, no data corruption, and no security issues were observed anywhere in this pass. However, 21 distinct issues were logged across the 6 prompts, including 3 Critical and 6 High-severity issues that remain fully Open as of Prompt 6: is_own_account_transfer false positives that can suppress up to 100% of a real account's reported outflows (B3-1); a zero-transaction account scoring as perfectly creditworthy (B5-2); and a deterministic Gemini-timeout bug that has caused the lender-brief's AI recommendation section to fail in every real call tested (B6-1). These three critical issues, plus the compounding lack of insufficient-data warnings on several endpoints (B3-3, B4-2, B6-4), mean a real user could currently be shown misleading headline figures (zero spending, perfect credit score) with no warning that the underlying data is either contaminated or absent. None of this blocks moving forward -- every issue degrades gracefully/silently rather than breaking the system, and the core calculation logic is sound -- but these issues should be fixed, or at minimum explicitly flagged to whoever consumes Integration Testing's results, before the Bank Analyzer is treated as trustworthy for real lending or financial decisions.
